slides.headline: AI JUST SCORED 151 ON MENSA'S IQ TEST, 3 CEO MOVES NOW

caption:
AI just scored 151 on the Mensa Norway IQ test. Three years ago it was
64. Here are the 3 CEO moves. 🧠

THE 151 WINDOW.

1) The payroll math

Three years ago, AI scored 64 on Mensa Norway's IQ test. Below the average human. One year later: average. The year after: genius. This week: 151, the highest score the test can produce. Your top analyst earns $120K to $180K a year. The thing that just broke the Mensa scale costs $20 a month. Which roles in your business are you still paying human-speed prices for?

2) The 90-day gap

Every CEO in your market is reading this same headline today. The ones who move in the next 90 days enter 2027 with a hard structural cost edge. The ones who wait spend 2028 catching up to a gap that's already compounding. Pick three roles in your business where the output is a document, a recommendation, or a decision. Those three are your first moves.

3) The decision layer

Most owners use AI to write emails. That's a to-do list move, and it barely shows up in the numbers. The CEOs pulling ahead are running pricing, acquisition, and retention strategy through AI first. Tonight, run this: "Here are my three biggest costs and three biggest revenue sources. What is the single most dangerous scenario for my margin over the next 12 months, and what should I do about it?" That question used to cost $500 an hour to answer.

SAVE THIS: the three moves before your board asks why you haven't made them yet.

AI's IQ trajectory is only three years old. Every business is now competing against something that outscores the smartest person in any room on every standard cognitive test. The window to build this into your operations before your competition does is getting shorter every month.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.
